questions_before_times: How many horses, their ages, and about how much each weighs
Has any horse ever kicked, bitten or struck at a person? (a yes sends the request to the owner first)
Shod or barefoot now, and what's needed: a trim, new shoes, a reset, or something corrective
How long since the last visit, and any lameness or a crack the owner knows about
The barn: a private barn, a boarding stable or a field, and a covered, level, dry place to work
safety_stop: a horse that is hurt, bleeding badly, down, in colic pain or can't put weight on a leg, right now
a person kicked, stepped on or bitten and hurt
a horse loose on a road or lost right now
a horse with hot, painful hooves that won't walk
a horse that can't be held safely
license: Usually none: most places license neither farriers nor horse shoeing. A farrier may hold a voluntary certification, which shows only as the business's own word. A city or county may ask for a business license. The state's or city's form says which.
